pages.title: Marking
pages.text:
Switch the pointer to $(l)Mark$() mode (Ctrl + scroll), then sneak + right-click to mark in order:$(br)
$(li)Work block: depot / basin / belt$(br)$(li)Input: a container$(br)$(li)Output: a container$(br)
$(italic)Only blocks with an item handler count as containers. $()

pages.title: Applying to a maid
pages.text:
When you're done, $(l)sneak + right-click the maid$(). The chat bar tells you which mode you got:$(br)
$(li)$(l)Full logistics$(): work block + input + output$(br)$(li)$(l)Process-only$(): only the work block$(br)
$(c)Only the work block is mandatory$().

pages.title: Process-only mode
pages.text:
If you only mark a work block, she processes whatever $(l)you$() put on it — no fetching, no output transfer.

Handy when robots or belts handle the logistics and you just want her to do the hammering.

$(italic)Note: if the output can be processed again by the same tool (log → stripped → planks), she'll keep going and spend durability each step. $()

pages.title: Marks are exclusive
pages.text:
A maid listens to $(l)either$() work targets $(l)or$() fluid targets, never both.

Applying fluid marks clears her work block / input / output, and vice versa. Switch back to the other mode and re-apply to change your mind.
